assertions.verbatim_quote: Rely on a centralized identity provider: You should manage user identities centrally through an identity provider (IdP). This makes it easier to manage access across multiple applications and services.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that user credentials are not managed via local individual IAM users with static access keys, but federated through AWS IAM Identity Center or external SAML 2.0/OIDC IdP.
assertions.rationale: Prevents credential sprawling and facilitates immediate single-point offboarding.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Require multi-factor authentication (MFA): Require MFA for all identities in your organization. MFA adds an extra layer of protection on top of a user name and password.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that IAM users and federated sessions require hardware token, TOTP, or FIDO2/WebAuthn MFA to authenticate.
assertions.rationale: Eliminates account takeover risk resulting from single-factor password compromise.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Grant least privilege: Enforce requirements across every interaction. Grant only the permissions required to perform a task.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that IAM policies do not use wildcard '*' actions or resources unless strictly scoped with conditions.
assertions.rationale: Restricts the blast radius in the event an identity or application token is hijacked.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Use temporary credentials: Use temporary credentials instead of long-term access keys. AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) provides short-term credentials.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that programmatic access across EC2, ECS, Lambda, and pipelines uses IAM roles and STS AssumeRole tokens with bounded session durations.
assertions.rationale: Eliminates static secret leakage in source repositories or configuration files.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Protect root credentials: The root user has complete access to all AWS resources in the account. Do not use the root user for everyday tasks, and secure it with multi-factor authentication.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that root account access keys do not exist and that console root login alerts trigger immediate security notifications.
assertions.rationale: Root user compromise leads to complete and unrecoverable account hijacking.

assertions.section: Identity and access management for Amazon S3
assertions.verbatim_quote: Use IAM roles for applications and AWS services that require Amazon S3 access: Do not embed AWS credentials in application code or on instances.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that application workloads interacting with S3 rely on IAM instance profiles or IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA).
assertions.rationale: Prevents credential hardcoding and ensures automatic credential rotation.

assertions.section: SEC04: Configure service and application logging
assertions.verbatim_quote: Enable AWS CloudTrail: Enable AWS CloudTrail across all Regions to capture management and data events. Store log files in an S3 bucket that is dedicated to log storage and protected from tampering.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that multi-Region CloudTrail is enabled in all accounts with log file validation and immutable S3 storage.
assertions.rationale: CloudTrail provides the foundational audit trail for all control plane interactions.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Protect log storage: Prevent modification or deletion of log files by using access control mechanisms, encryption, and object locking.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that CloudTrail and VPC Flow Logs S3 buckets enforce MFA Delete or Object Lock WORM retention.
assertions.rationale: Prevents an attacker from deleting evidence of an active breach or intrusion.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Enable automated threat detection: Use services like Amazon GuardDuty to continuously monitor for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that Amazon GuardDuty is enabled across all active AWS accounts and Regions.
assertions.rationale: Applies machine learning and threat intelligence to identify compromised instances, keys, or S3 anomalies.

assertions.section: Logging and monitoring in Amazon S3
assertions.verbatim_quote: Enable server access logging: Server access logging provides detailed records for the requests that are made to a bucket.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that sensitive and regulated S3 buckets have server access logging or CloudTrail S3 data events enabled.
assertions.rationale: Provides visibility into read, write, and delete operations on individual S3 objects.

assertions.section: [S3.11] S3 buckets should have event notifications enabled
assertions.verbatim_quote: This control checks whether an Amazon S3 bucket has event notifications enabled. The control fails if notifications are not configured.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that critical S3 buckets publish event notifications (SNS, SQS, EventBridge) upon ObjectCreated or ObjectRemoved events.
assertions.rationale: Enables real-time automated security ingestion and forensic pipelines.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Capture VPC Flow Logs: Enable VPC Flow Logs to monitor IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in your VPC.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that all active VPCs have flow logging enabled and routed to CloudWatch Logs or centralized S3 bucket.
assertions.rationale: Critical for detecting network port scans, unauthorized data egress, and C2 traffic.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Use Amazon S3 Block Public Access: Amazon S3 Block Public Access settings override any other S3 permissions, allowing you to limit public access to your buckets and objects.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that all four Block Public Access flags (BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets) are set to true at both account and bucket level.
assertions.rationale: Provides a definitive barrier against accidental public data leaks caused by misconfigured bucket policies or ACLs.

assertions.section: [S3.1] S3 general purpose buckets should have block public access settings enabled
assertions.verbatim_quote: This control checks whether your Amazon S3 general purpose buckets have block public access settings enabled.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify automated compliance scan flags any general-purpose S3 bucket with BPA disabled.
assertions.rationale: Security Hub compliance baseline requirement across CIS and AWS FSBP benchmarks.

assertions.section: [S3.5] S3 general purpose buckets should require requests to use TLS
assertions.verbatim_quote: This control checks whether Amazon S3 general purpose buckets require requests to use Transport Layer Security (TLS). The control fails if the bucket policy does not require HTTPS.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify bucket policy contains an explicit Deny statement where 'aws:SecureTransport' condition equals 'false'.
assertions.rationale: Enforces in-transit encryption and prevents plaintext HTTP sniffing or man-in-the-middle tampering.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Encrypt data at rest: Encrypt data stored in Amazon S3 using server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3), AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS), or customer-provided keys (SSE-C).
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that all S3 buckets have default server-side encryption enabled using AES-256 (SSE-S3) or AWS KMS.
assertions.rationale: Guarantees physical and media-level data confidentiality on underlying storage hardware.

assertions.section: [S3.8] S3 general purpose buckets should block public write access
assertions.verbatim_quote: This control checks whether your Amazon S3 general purpose buckets block public write access.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that anonymous or unauthenticated PUT/POST requests to S3 buckets are explicitly rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden.
assertions.rationale: Prevents unauthorized actors from writing malicious content, ransomware, or untrusted payloads into the bucket.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Enable versioning: Versioning protects against accidental overwrites and deletions by keeping multiple variants of an object in the same bucket.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that S3 bucket versioning status is 'Enabled' for critical data repositories.
assertions.rationale: Enables instant point-in-time recovery from accidental data corruption or rogue delete operations.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Enable MFA Delete: MFA Delete adds another layer of security if your bucket versioning is enabled. It requires authentication with an MFA device to change bucket versioning or permanently delete an object version.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that bucket configuration has 'MfaDelete: Enabled' on buckets containing regulated or non-reproducible records.
assertions.rationale: Prevents rogue administrators or stolen root/admin keys from deleting backup versions without physical token.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Use Amazon S3 Object Lock: Object Lock can help you meet regulatory requirements that require Write Once, Read Many (WORM) storage, or add an extra layer of protection against object changes and deletions.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that compliance buckets have Object Lock enabled in Compliance or Governance mode with retention periods configured.
assertions.rationale: Guarantees SEC Rule 17a-4, FINRA, and CFTC regulatory compliance for immutable financial and audit logs.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Disable access control lists (ACLs): AWS recommends that you disable ACLs and use bucket policies to control access to your buckets and objects.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify bucket ownership controls have ObjectOwnership set to 'BucketOwnerEnforced'.
assertions.rationale: Simplifies authorization by making IAM and Bucket Policies the single source of access truth.

assertions.section: [S3.17] S3 general purpose buckets should have cross-Region replication enabled
assertions.verbatim_quote: This control checks whether cross-Region replication is enabled for your Amazon S3 general purpose buckets.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify replication configuration specifies a target bucket in a geographically distinct AWS Region with KMS key re-encryption.
assertions.rationale: Ensures disaster recovery resilience against regional outages or disasters.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Develop incident response playbooks: Create step-by-step playbooks for your organization's most common security incidents to ensure consistent, effective response.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify documented, runnable playbooks exist for credential exposure, ransomware detection, and unauthorized access.
assertions.rationale: Reduces mean time to remediate (MTTR) and prevents chaotic ad-hoc triage during a critical breach.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Automate containment: Use automated scripts or AWS Step Functions to quarantine compromised resources, revoke credentials, and isolate network segments.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify automated response can detach IAM policies, apply an isolating security group, and take forensic EBS snapshots upon GuardDuty high-severity finding.
assertions.rationale: Stops lateral threat movement within seconds without waiting for human operator intervention.

assertions.section: SEC06: Protect compute and network boundaries
assertions.verbatim_quote: Implement layered defense: Apply security controls at multiple layers of your workload, such as edge networks, VPC endpoints, and compute instances.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that traffic to S3 from VPCs traverses AWS PrivateLink or VPC Endpoints without traversing the public internet.
assertions.rationale: Eliminates exposure to internet routing vulnerabilities and DNS spoofing.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Enforce inspection and protection: Use network firewalls, such as AWS Network Firewall or web application firewalls like AWS WAF, to inspect incoming and outgoing traffic.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify internet-facing web endpoints are protected by AWS WAF with rate-limiting and OWASP Top 10 managed rule groups.
assertions.rationale: Shields applications against SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and automated bot scraping.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Run game days: Regularly test your incident response procedures through simulated events and game days to identify gaps in tools and processes.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that tabletop exercises and automated chaos/security game days are conducted and documented annually.
assertions.rationale: Validates that personnel, alerting channels, and automated playbooks operate as designed under pressure.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Regularly audit credentials: Audit and rotate credentials periodically. Identify and deactivate unused credentials to reduce the risk of compromised credentials.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify IAM credential report is generated regularly and keys older than 90 days or unused for 45 days are disabled.
assertions.rationale: Reduces exposure window for forgotten, abandoned, or stale developer access tokens.

assertions.section: [S3.13] S3 general purpose buckets should have lifecycle policies configured
assertions.verbatim_quote: This control checks whether an Amazon S3 general purpose bucket has a lifecycle configuration rule. The control fails if no lifecycle rules are active.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify S3 bucket has lifecycle rules transitioning stale data to Glacier or expiring incomplete multipart uploads.
assertions.rationale: Ensures adherence to corporate data retention periods and reduces attack surface of stale data.

assertions.verbatim_quote: Use service control policies (SCPs): Use SCPs in AWS Organizations to enforce central permission guardrails across all accounts in your organization.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify SCP attached to organizational root denies member accounts from disabling CloudTrail, GuardDuty, or S3 Block Public Access.
assertions.rationale: Prevents member account administrators from disabling critical corporate security controls.

assertions.section: Classifying sensitive data with Amazon Macie
assertions.verbatim_quote: Use Amazon Macie to discover sensitive data: Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and protect sensitive data in Amazon S3.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify automated discovery scans identify and alert on PII, PHI, financial records, or credentials stored in S3.
assertions.rationale: Prevents accidental exposure of regulated personal data and intellectual property.

assertions.section: [S3.12] S3 general purpose buckets should prohibit ACLs
assertions.verbatim_quote: This control checks whether Amazon S3 general purpose buckets prohibit access control lists (ACLs). The control passes if Object Ownership is set to Bucket owner enforced.
assertions.verification_criteria: Verify that attempts to apply legacy S3 ACLs return an AccessControlListNotSupported error.
assertions.rationale: Eliminates legacy ACL misconfigurations that historically caused public data exposures.
